findings.claim_source_sentence: Scientific communities should be able to define their own machine-actionable templates for metadata that encode these "rich," discipline-specific elements.
findings.study_system: Metadata templates for FAIR data (CEDAR / FAIRware Workbench)

findings.claim: FAIR-Checker is a web tool using Semantic Web standards (SPARQL/SHACL) to automatically assess and improve the FAIRness of digital resources' metadata.
findings.claim_source_sentence: As a first step to address these issues, we propose FAIR-Checker, a web-based tool to assess the FAIRness of metadata presented by digital resources.
findings.study_system: Bioinformatics digital resources / software metadata (FAIR-Checker)

findings.claim: A review analyzed over 300 data-stewardship tools for their utility and relevance to life-science research data management.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Over 300 tools were analyzed in this study, assessing their utility, relevance to data stewardship, and applicability within the life sciences domain.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Over 300 tools were analyzed in this study, assessing their utility, relevance to data stewardship, and applicability within the life sciences domain.
findings.study_system: Data stewardship tools in life science (review)

findings.claim: Limited machine-interpretability of population-health metadata hinders discovery and reuse; a three-stage framework renders metadata machine-readable to improve FAIRness.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, the limited accessibility and machine-interpretability of existing metadata for population health data hinder effective data discovery and reuse.
findings.study_system: Population health data metadata (Malawi/Kenya IDSR; machine-readable metadata framework)

findings.claim: The FAIR Guiding Principles lack specificity on semantic interoperability; the authors propose linguistic-based extensions and a FAIR ecosystem of services to close the gap.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The FAIR Guiding Principles lack specificity regarding semantic interoperability.
findings.study_system: FAIR principles / semantic interoperability (conceptual model)

findings.claim: A data-value evaluation model scored 10 open medical-science data platforms, finding that overall utilization of these data values remains limited.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Data from 10 domestic and international open platforms were collected and empirically analyzed using the entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution technique.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Data from 10 domestic and international open platforms were collected and empirically analyzed using the entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution technique.
findings.study_system: Medical science data open platforms (data value evaluation model)

findings.claim: Open, FAIR-style data sharing is counterbalanced by Indigenous Research Sovereignty, which asserts Indigenous Peoples' rights and self-determination over data generated about them.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our exploration of Indigenous Research Sovereignty, or Indigenous self-determination in the context of research activities, has been focused on the relationship between Indigenous Data Sovereignty and efforts to describe Indigenous Peoples' Rights in data.
findings.study_system: Indigenous Data Sovereignty / research governance (conceptual)

findings.claim: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance were developed to complement FAIR: FAIR facilitates data sharing, but Indigenous Data Sovereignty demands greater Indigenous control and oversight over how data are shared.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, the Indigenous Data Sovereignty movement advocates for greater Indigenous control and oversight in order to share data on Indigenous Peoples' terms.
findings.study_system: Biomedical/genetic data governance for Indigenous Peoples (CARE + tribal research codes)

findings.claim: Because much research data are generated from research activities, Indigenous research governance and Indigenous data governance overlap, and CARE is used to set expectations for research legislation and policy.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Given that much data are generated from research, Indigenous research governance and Indigenous Data Governance overlap.
findings.study_system: Indigenous research governance / data governance (US tribal legislation)

findings.claim: The CARE principles were developed to protect Indigenous data sovereignty in an era of open/big data, but there are few worked examples of how to translate them into practice.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The CARE principles for Indigenous data governance-Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility and Ethics-were developed to protect Indigenous data sovereignty, but there are few examples of how to translate these principles into practice.
findings.study_system: Indigenous environmental program data (Australian ranger groups, CARE case study)

findings.claim: The SEEDS principles were articulated to govern the increasingly sensitive linkage of Indigenous population health data, foregrounding self-determination and data stewardship.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The SEEDS Principles emerge as collective report that outlines a living and expanding set of guiding principles that: 1) prioritizes Indigenous Peoples' right to Self-determination; 2) makes space for Indigenous Peoples to Exercise sovereignty; 3) adheres to Ethical protocols; 4) acknowledges and respects Data stewardship and governance, and; 5) works to Support reconciliation between Indigenous nations and settler states.
findings.study_system: Indigenous population health data linkage (Canada, New Zealand, US)

findings.claim: A review of seven Australian primary-care datasets found only two adequately captured Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander chronic disease at national scale, and none captured both mainstream and Aboriginal community-controlled clinics, reflecting weak alignment with Indigenous Data Sovereignty.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Only two datasets reported on chronic disease, collected data nationally and captured a substantial number of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We identified seven datasets.
findings.study_system: Australian general-practice datasets for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander chronic-disease care

findings.claim: A legal-epidemiology review of research legislation from 26 US tribes, framed by CARE, identified facilitators and barriers to securing benefits from (genomic) research and gaps in Responsibility and Ethics.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Using a legal epidemiology approach, the paper discusses findings from a review of Tribal research legislation, policy, and administrative materials from 26 tribes in the US.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Using a legal epidemiology approach, the paper discusses findings from a review of Tribal research legislation, policy, and administrative materials from 26 tribes in the US.
findings.study_system: US tribal research legislation and genomic-research benefit sharing (CARE)

findings.claim: Public availability of large-scale datasets (e.g., the ABCD Study) creates both opportunities and challenges for American Indian populations, motivating five data-use recommendations grounded in Indigenous Data Sovereignty and Governance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The public availability of data from large-scale studies creates both opportunities and challenges when studying mental health within AIAN populations.
findings.study_system: Publicly available large-scale study data (ABCD Study) for American Indian/Alaska Native populations

findings.claim: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are absent from or under-represented in human reference genomes and genomic datasets, and building Indigenous data sovereignty and governance into research is required to protect their rights and collective interests.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Yet, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are absent from, or under-represented within, human reference genome resources, genomic studies, cancer studies, cancer cell lines, patient-derived xenografts and cancer clinical trials.
findings.study_system: Genomic reference resources and precision-cancer data (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander)

findings.claim: FAIR principles for research software were recently proposed as an extension of the original FAIR data principles, and FAIR Digital Objects enable discovery and reuse of research objects including computational workflows by humans and machines.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Based on the concepts of the original FAIR principles for research data, FAIR principles for research software were recently proposed.
findings.study_system: Multi-omics data-analysis workflow packaged as a FAIR Digital Object (RO-Crate/WorkflowHub)

findings.claim: A global working group systematically applied both FAIR data and FAIR software principles to computational workflows and issued adoption recommendations, treating workflows as first-class digital research objects.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The Workflows Community Initiative’s FAIR Workflows Working Group (WCI-FW), a global and open community of researchers and developers working with computational workflows across disciplines and domains, has systematically addressed the application of both FAIR data and software principles to computational workflows.
findings.study_system: Computational workflows / FAIR principles (Workflows Community Initiative)

findings.claim: Workflow Run RO-Crate captures machine-actionable provenance of computational workflow executions and was implemented across six workflow systems, enabling interoperable comparison of runs from heterogeneous systems.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We describe the model, its alignment to standards such as W3C PROV, and its implementation in six workflow systems.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We describe the model, its alignment to standards such as W3C PROV, and its implementation in six workflow systems.
findings.study_system: Computational workflow provenance (Workflow Run RO-Crate)

findings.claim: Reproducibility alone does not guarantee reuse or new knowledge; users must still expend considerable effort to understand data and code, motivating richer reusability packages (Data-to-Knowledge Packages).
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, reproducibility alone does not guarantee these benefits.
findings.study_system: Reproducible computational research reuse (hydrological use case)

findings.claim: In a biodiversity digital-twin project, tools like RO-Crate operationalise FAIR principles for metadata packaging and standardisation across ten prototype digital twins.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Critically, we highlight the opportunities for dynamic adaptation, modular workflows, and cross-domain collaboration, detailing how tools like Research Object Crate (RO-Crate) operationalise FAIR principles for metadata packaging and standardisation.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The BioDT project developed ten prototype digital twins addressing a critical range of challenges, including grassland and forest dynamics, bird monitoring, ecosystem services, and crop wild relative genetic resources.
findings.study_system: FAIR Digital Twins for biodiversity (BioDT, RO-Crate metadata)

findings.claim: The TRUST Principles (Transparency, Responsibility, User focus, Sustainability, Technology) were introduced because repositories must earn the trust of their communities and demonstrate reliable, capable data management.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Repositories must earn the trust of the communities they intend to serve and demonstrate that they are reliable and capable of appropriately managing the data they hold.
findings.study_system: Trustworthy digital repositories (TRUST Principles, foundational statement)

findings.claim: A crosswalk of three established maturity-assessment approaches (CoreTrustSeal, Data Stewardship Maturity Matrix, and FAIR) found strong correlations in discovery, accessibility, interoperability, and usability, but that their complexity yields highly variable inferred mappings.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Strong correlations are found in data discovery, accessibility, interoperability, and usability due to overlapping requirements in digital object management.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In this article, we outline the commonalities and distinctions of three established assessment approaches: i) CoreTrustSeal Trustworthy Data Repositories Requirements, ii) Data Stewardship Maturity Matrix, and iii) FAIR Guiding Principles.
findings.study_system: Repository stewardship maturity assessment approaches (CoreTrustSeal/DSMM/FAIR crosswalk)

findings.claim: Although hundreds of Trustworthy Digital Repositories are certified, there is no evidence certification actually improves preservation; a content analysis of 91 certified repository websites examined how certification is communicated.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Even though hundreds of repositories are currently certified, we do not know if audit and certification of TDRs actually matters.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Using findings from a content analysis of 91 TDR-certified repository websites, this research examines: 1) written statements about TDR status, 2) the presence of TDR seals and their location, 3) whether the seals hyperlink to additional certification information, 4) the extent to which the certification process is explained, and 5) whether audit reports are shared.
findings.study_system: Certified trustworthy digital repository websites (content analysis)

findings.claim: In an online survey of computable biomedical knowledge repositories, all 13 responding organizations reported varying adherence to TRUST-aligned policies, but User-Focus and Sustainability practices were the least common.
findings.claim_source_sentence: All 13 respondents indicated to different degrees adherence to policies that convey TRUST.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Descriptive statistics methods were applied to data from 13 responding organizations, to identify common practices and policies instantiating the TRUST principles of Transparency, Responsibility, User Focus, Sustainability, and Technology.
findings.study_system: Computable biomedical knowledge repositories (TRUST principles survey)

findings.claim: An OFCT (Open, FAIR, Citable, Trustworthy) instrument applied to eight biomedical repositories found little explicit acknowledgment of any of the principles, though most repositories provided at least some support for their tenets.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, although there was little explicit acknowledgment of any of the OFCT principles in our sample, the majority of repositories provided at least some support for their tenets.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: They are joined by principles governing open science, data citation and trustworthiness, all of which are important aspects for biomedical data repositories to support.
findings.study_system: Biomedical data repositories (OFCT alignment tool, dkNET)

findings.claim: Building a FAIR data ecosystem (e.g., the European Open Science Cloud) requires data infrastructures to evolve services spanning certification, stewardship, costs, and rewards, per prioritized community recommendations.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The recommendations cover a broad area of topics, including certification, infrastructure components, stewardship, costs, rewards, collaboration, training, support, and data management.
findings.study_system: FAIR data ecosystem services (EOSC; FAIRsFAIR/RDA/OpenAIRE workshops)

findings.claim: Software is now recognized as a key research output requiring the same transparency and disclosure as data, and the paper gives publishers structured guidance to implement software and data citation for credit and reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Software is now recognized as a key research result and resource, requiring the same level of transparency, accessibility, and disclosure as data.
findings.study_system: Scholarly publishing workflows for software and data citation (credit/attribution)

findings.claim: Analysis of download logs from a Swiss social-science data archive found realized reuse is highly concentrated: downloads focus heavily on a small share of datasets and most users download only one dataset.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The findings show that quantitative datasets are downloaded increasingly from the digital archive and that downloads focus heavily on a small share of the datasets.
findings.study_system: Social-science data archive reuse (Swiss digital data archive log analysis)

findings.claim: Establishing the first US palliative-care qualitative data repository required co-designed, tailored deposit guidelines and access controls, and initially recruited ten projects to share data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We describe the processes used to develop this repository, called the PCRC-QDR, as well as our outreach and education among the palliative care researcher community, which led to the first ten projects to share the data in the new repository.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We describe the processes used to develop this repository, called the PCRC-QDR, as well as our outreach and education among the palliative care researcher community, which led to the first ten projects to share the data in the new repository.
findings.study_system: Qualitative palliative-care data repository (PCRC-QDR, NIH DMS Policy)

findings.claim: Qualitative data sharing raises distinctive challenges - consent for scholarly reuse, legal/ethical sharing, and data that cannot be de-identified - that repositories and academic libraries must help researchers address.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This paper describes how data repositories and academic libraries can partner with researchers to support three challenges associated with qualitative data sharing: (1) obtaining informed consent from participants for data sharing and scholarly reuse; (2) ensuring that qualitative data are legally and ethically shared; and (3) sharing data that cannot be deidentified.
findings.study_system: Qualitative research data sharing (repositories and academic libraries)

findings.claim: Long-term preservation of biomedical data is proposed via an Open Archival Information System model of six functional entities, with data stewards engaged early in the digital data life cycle.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The actions involve utilizing an Open Archival Information System model comprised of six functional entities: Ingest, Access, Data Management, Archival Storage, Administration and Preservation Planning.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The actions involve utilizing an Open Archival Information System model comprised of six functional entities: Ingest, Access, Data Management, Archival Storage, Administration and Preservation Planning.
findings.study_system: Long-term preservation of biomedical research data (OAIS model)

findings.claim: A DSpace-based demonstrator repository for individual clinical-trial data met 14 of 19 (74%) predefined quality requirements, showing generalist repository software can support sensitive data with metadata and identifiers.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Generally, the performance of the DSpace demonstrator repository in supporting sensitive personal data such as that from clinical trials was strong, with 14 requirements demonstrated (74%), including the necessary support for metadata and identifiers.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Generally, the performance of the DSpace demonstrator repository in supporting sensitive personal data such as that from clinical trials was strong, with 14 requirements demonstrated (74%), including the necessary support for metadata and identifiers.
findings.study_system: Clinical-trial individual participant data repository (DSpace demonstrator)

findings.claim: In a survey of about 250 researchers, most affirmed formal reference-list citation as the proper credit for dataset creators, but few expected published data to be peer-reviewed - although peer-reviewed data enjoyed greater trust and prestige.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Formal citation in the reference list was affirmed by most respondents as the proper way to credit dataset creators.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: To bring this important yet neglected perspective into the conversation, we surveyed ∼ 250 researchers across the sciences and social sciences- asking what expectations"data publication" raises and what features would be useful to evaluate the trustworthiness, evaluate the impact, and enhance the prestige of a data publication.
findings.study_system: Researcher perceptions of data publication and data peer review (survey)

findings.claim: Next-generation MS proteomics framework argues FAIR data practices, proteoform biology and AI analytics are usually pursued independently and should be integrated so FAIR/standardization provides machine-actionable foundations.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite these advancements, FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) data practices, proteoform biology, and AI analytics are often pursued independently.
findings.study_system: mass spectrometry-based proteomics datasets
findings.evidence: Perspective/framework paper on FAIR + proteoform-resolved reproducible proteomics; includes a minimal community reproducibility checklist.

findings.claim: Proteomics community has embraced data sharing but dataset metadata provision (biological sample and experimental design level) remains limited, hampering large-scale reuse; existing standards (SDRF-Proteomics) have limited adoption.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The proteomics community has fully embraced data sharing, yet data set metadata provision remains limited, especially at the level of the biological samples and experimental design.
findings.study_system: public proteomics datasets (ProteomeXchange)
findings.evidence: Second sentence: 'Although standards such as Sample and Data Relationship Format for Proteomics (SDRF-Proteomics) and supporting tools are already available, their adoption remains limited.'

findings.claim: European photon and neutron research infrastructures produce up to 1 PByte/day; making all such data FAIR requires enormous effort (storage, metadata schemes, pipelines) and FAIR is now an EU-funding requirement.
findings.claim_source_sentence: They produce large data volumes of up to 1 PByte per day in some cases.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: They produce large data volumes of up to 1 PByte per day in some cases.
findings.study_system: photon and neutron large-scale research infrastructures (Europe)
findings.evidence: White paper on shared user/RI accountability for FAIR data in photon-neutron facilities.

findings.claim: Review of metadata from 71 UAV/drone datasets in public repositories found current practices often lack essential details (sensors, processing steps, licensing), limiting FAIR compliance; survey of >70 users informed key metadata requirements.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We assessed how UAV data is currently published by reviewing metadata from 71 datasets in public repositories.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We assessed how UAV data is currently published by reviewing metadata from 71 datasets in public repositories.
findings.study_system: UAV/drone datasets in public repositories
findings.evidence: Second sentence: 'However, current practices often lack essential details about sensors, processing steps, and licensing, which limits FAIR compliance.'

findings.claim: FAIR m-BIDS extends the BIDS standard by shifting granularity to individual data entities, assigning each brain data file an independent Global Unique Identifier Key to enable cross-study/cross-modality integration and improve FAIR compliance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Each brain data file receives an independent GUId-Key (Global Unique Identifier Key), enabling researchers to select and integrate data items from different modalities and studies into customized multimodal datasets.
findings.study_system: multimodal brain imaging data (BIDS extension)

findings.claim: Proposes a semantic FAIRness framework leveraging FAIR principles and semantic technologies for integrating heterogeneous COVID-19 genomic/clinical/epidemiological data in the UAE, but the framework as a whole is not yet implemented or empirically evaluated.
findings.claim_source_sentence: While selected components of the framework build on prior proof-of-concept implementations, the framework as a whole has not yet been fully implemented or empirically evaluated.
findings.study_system: COVID-19 genomic/clinical/epidemiological datasets (UAE)

findings.claim: Raman spectroscopy data landscape remains fragmented with many initiatives developed in isolation, limiting interoperability; standardized formats, metadata schemas and domain ontologies are needed for machine-actionability and a proposed open/FAIR ecosystem.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite these advances, the field remains fragmented, with many initiatives developed in isolation, limiting interoperability and slowing progress.
findings.study_system: Raman spectroscopy data
findings.evidence: Emphasizes standardized data formats, metadata schemas and domain-specific ontologies for machine-actionability and database federation.

findings.claim: Assessment of FAIR adoption across 14 Italian environmental research infrastructures (atmosphere, marine, biosphere, geosphere) revealed significant heterogeneity in implemented practices with convergence efforts strongest in the marine subdomain.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The findings reveal significant heterogeneity in the implemented practices, with ongoing efforts to converge on common strategies, particularly in the marine subdomain.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This study investigates the adoption of the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) principles by 14 environmental research infrastructures (RIs) operating at the Italian level.
findings.study_system: environmental research infrastructures (Italy)

findings.claim: Cross-sectional survey of 44 hemoglobinopathy centers (22 countries) found half had basic metadata, only 20% used ontologies, none implemented common data models (OMOP/CDISC); despite limited FAIR compliance, 86% were willing to join federated sharing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite limited FAIR compliance, most respondents expressed willingness to participate in federated (86%) or centralized (68%) data sharing.
findings.effect_size: 20% used ontologies; none used OMOP/CDISC; 86% willing to federate
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Half of the centers reported basic metadata documentation, 20% used recognized ontologies, and none implemented common data models such as OMOP or CDISC, and only isolated mentions of HL7 FHIR were observed.
findings.study_system: hemoglobinopathy research centers (HELIOS network, 22 countries)

findings.claim: Data-sharing maturity is highly discipline-dependent (astronomy/bioinformatics have long histories; many fields do not); a detailed analysis of existing web-based systems focuses on making mathematical research data FAIR.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Some disciplines, such as astronomy or bioinformatics, already have a long history of sharing data; many others do not.
findings.study_system: mathematical research data sharing systems

findings.claim: Analysis of 192 publications from two EU aquatic mesocosm projects found more datasets published alongside papers (103) than in a repository alone (17), and 32.6% of papers achieved the highest FAIR scores (7 or 8), indicating relatively high transparency.
findings.claim_source_sentence: More data sets were published alongside scientific papers (103) than in a data repository alone (17).
findings.effect_size: 32.6% of papers achieved highest FAIR scores (7 or 8 of 8)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Regarding FAIR principles, 32.6% of papers achieved the highest scores (7 or 8), emphasizing a high data transparency relative to other disciplines.
findings.study_system: aquatic mesocosm experiment publications (EU)

findings.claim: Argues that EOSC's advanced FAIR-data services depend on intrinsically limited resources (e.g., data-processing algorithms) so access will be competitive, and governance/funding challenge EOSC's effective openness as a common good.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In particular, we emphasize that key resources as required to access and exploit EOSC's advanced FAIR-data services - such as data-processing algorithms - are, in fact, intrinsically limited and the access will be competitive.
findings.study_system: European Open Science Cloud (EOSC)

findings.claim: The INGV Data Registry is a centralized, curated, metadata-only infrastructure where each record is assigned a DOI and mapped to international standards; a three-tiered validation workflow plus PID integration (ORCIDs, RORs) ensures high-quality interoperable metadata.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We demonstrate how a three-tiered validation workflow, combined with the integration of Persistent Identifiers (ORCIDs, RORs), ensures high-quality, interoperable metadata.
findings.effect_size: hundreds of records, each assigned a DOI
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The Registry operates as a dynamic ecosystem that manages hundreds of records, each assigned to a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) and mapped to international standards.
findings.study_system: geophysics/volcanology metadata (INGV, Italy)

findings.claim: Developed a maturity model framework of six domains (governance, operations/performance, three technical domains, and outreach) for federating Trusted Research Environments, aligning with DARE UK's SATRE and Federated Architecture Blueprint.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Merging synonymous and related components resulted in a maturity model framework consisting of six discreet domains that are required for optimal TRE federation.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Merging synonymous and related components resulted in a maturity model framework consisting of six discreet domains that are required for optimal TRE federation.
findings.study_system: Trusted Research Environments (federated networks, UK/international)

findings.claim: Developed Maggot, a web-based tool to locally manage a data catalog using high-level metadata aligned with FAIR principles, enabling metadata crosswalks to repository schemas and supporting the future EOSC FAIR Web of Data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We developed Maggot (Metadata Aggregation on Data Storage), a web-based tool to locally manage a data catalog using high-level metadata.
findings.study_system: research data management / metadata tooling
findings.evidence: Enables metadata crosswalks: 'generated metadata can be converted to the schema used by a specific data repository or be exported using a format suitable for data collection by third-party applications.'

findings.claim: First Italian national survey (2023, 77 valid responses) mapping data stewards found most institutions employ staff performing stewardship tasks but rarely formally recognized with that title; commonest tasks were FAIR support, DMP writing, researcher training, and policy consultancy.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Results indicate that most institutions employ staff performing data management support tasks which map to the definition of data stewardship, though these professionals are rarely formally recognised with that title.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Data cleaning was performed on the 77 valid entries collected (out of 88 responses) before conducting the descriptive analyses.
findings.study_system: data stewards at universities/research institutions (Italy)

findings.claim: Analysis of European public human genomic data infrastructures argues the central challenge is no longer building platforms but aligning heterogeneous regulatory interpretations, metadata models, and trust frameworks across jurisdictions for federated, privacy-preserving reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We argue that the central challenge is no longer building individual platforms, but aligning heterogeneous regulatory interpretations, metadata models, and trust frameworks across jurisdictions.
findings.study_system: human genomic data infrastructures (Europe)

findings.claim: Evaluated ORCID coverage at two German research institutions across external PID data sources (FREYA PID Graph, OpenAlex, ORCID); coverage is still not sufficient for standard automated PID-based reporting but can already feed institutional CRIS.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Although the current level of coverage of researcher IDs which could automatically be mapped is still not sufficient to use persistent identifier-based extraction for standard (automated) reporting, it can already be a valuable input for institutional CRIS.
findings.effect_size: substantial differences in ORCID coverage between institutions and data sources
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Substantial differences can be found for ORCID coverage between both institutions and for each institution regarding the various external data sources.
findings.study_system: ORCID/PID coverage at German research institutions (UOS, TIB)

findings.claim: Analysis of the 153 largest Crossref publishers and four manuscript submission systems found some systems better suited to capturing certain metadata elements, but publishers using the same system differ widely, so technology is not the only barrier to metadata completeness.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, there are always cases where publishers using the same system differ widely in the level of metadata they register, suggesting that technology is not the only prohibiting factor and other considerations are at play.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We have looked at the 153 publishers with the largest amounts of publications in Crossref and concentrate on the four most commonly used systems: Editorial Manager, ScholarOne, Open Journal Systems (OJS) and eJournalPress.
findings.study_system: publication metadata completeness in Crossref

findings.claim: Identifies significant gaps in current practices and infrastructure that prevent accurate provenance tracking, reproducibility, and attribution for physical samples; ESIP developed author guidance for publishing open research using physical samples.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, there are significant gaps in current practices and infrastructure that prevent accurate provenance tracking, reproducibility, and attribution.
findings.study_system: physical samples in Earth and environmental sciences

findings.claim: Over a million taxonomic names were matched to DOIs/PIDs across three databases (Index Fungorum, IPNI, ION) - about 36% of names for which publication data are available - and a knowledge graph uses researcher ORCID ids to link names, publications and authors.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Over a million names have been matched to DOIs or other persistent identifiers for taxonomic publications.
findings.effect_size: ~36% of names for which publication data are available
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This represents approximately 36% of names for which publication data are available.
findings.study_system: taxonomic name / biodiversity databases (Index Fungorum, IPNI, ION)

findings.claim: Survey of 118 palaeontological/Earth science databases found ~85% of community-curated databases have lifespans under 15 years, with peaks in database loss tied to 5-year funding cycles, putting decades of volunteered-data investment at risk.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We show that approximately 85% of all community-curated databases have lifespans of less than 15 years, putting decades of investment at risk.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We show that approximately 85% of all community-curated databases have lifespans of less than 15 years, putting decades of investment at risk.
findings.study_system: palaeontological / Earth science databases
findings.evidence: Advocates sustained funding models, institutional support, and modular backend architectures for database longevity.

findings.claim: Manual curation and harmonization of metadata from 212,027 omics samples across 468 studies in two repositories (curatedMetagenomicData, cBioPortal) consolidated redundant information and increased completeness of major attributes, demonstrating the value of retrospective metadata improvement.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Through systematic ontology mapping, we consolidated redundant, dispersed information into far fewer harmonized columns, reduced unique values, and increased the completeness of major attributes.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We performed comprehensive manual curation and harmonization of metadata, such as participant characteristics and study conditions, from 212 027 omics samples across 468 studies in two repositories: curatedMetagenomicData (93 studies, 22 588 samples) and cBioPortal (375 studies, 189 438 samples).
findings.study_system: metagenomic and cancer genomic metadata repositories

findings.claim: The EU INCISIVE federated pan-European cancer imaging repository developed a data validation framework assessing clinical (meta)data and imaging across five dimensions - completeness, validity, consistency, integrity, and fairness - to pre-validate data before AI use.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We propose a data validation framework to assess clinical (meta)data and imaging data across five dimensions: completeness, validity, consistency, integrity, and fairness.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We propose a data validation framework to assess clinical (meta)data and imaging data across five dimensions: completeness, validity, consistency, integrity, and fairness.
findings.study_system: cancer imaging repository (EU INCISIVE)

findings.claim: Ten focus groups with 32 physical-collection managers found collections attempt to use universal metadata and storage standards for discoverability, but interdisciplinary collections and derived-data reuse require more investment to increase reusability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Results indicated that physical collections attempt to use universal metadata and data storage standards to increase discoverability, but interdisciplinary physical collections and derived data reuse require more investments to increase reusability of these invaluable items.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Ten focus groups were conducted with thirty-two participants across several physical collection communities.
findings.study_system: physical collection managers (cross-domain)

findings.claim: FAIRification (FHIR transformation) of rare-disease EHR data across 24 German UMCs induced data-quality issues: the FAIR/FHIR dataset contained 1988 DQ issues (1977 completeness) versus fewer in a direct export; 68% were resolved, and completeness indicators proved crucial.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found a higher number of DQ issues in FHIR-DS than in EXP-DS.
findings.effect_size: 1977 completeness issues induced by FAIRification; 68% resolved
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Specifically, FHIR-DS contained 1988 distinct DQ issues: nine ambiguous RD cases, two missing data items, and 1977 completeness issues induced by the FAIRification processes.
findings.study_system: rare-disease EHR data (German MII / CORD-MI)

findings.claim: Developed an SPHN RDF Schema extension for standardized, structured medical imaging metadata built on FAIR principles and established standards (DICOM, SNOMED CT), linking imaging metadata to clinical data to close interoperability gaps.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Built on the FAIR (Findable Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles and established standards like DICOM and SNOMED CT, this extension models essential imaging information and links it to related clinical data, such as diagnoses, patient visits, and biosamples.
findings.study_system: medical imaging metadata (Swiss Personalized Health Network)

findings.claim: Developed and validated an open pharmacogenetics data model in openEHR for semantic interoperability, achieving international consensus via peer review by 24 experts from 10 countries and bidirectional mapping to HL7 FHIR.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The model underwent two rounds of structured peer review involving 24 experts from 10 countries.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The model underwent two rounds of structured peer review involving 24 experts from 10 countries.
findings.study_system: pharmacogenetics clinical data model (openEHR/FHIR)

findings.claim: Systematic review scoring common data models (i2b2, Sentinel, PCORnet, OMOP) and data standards (CDA, HL7v2, FHIR, openEHR) found OMOP CDM and FHIR scored best overall, but concludes no single global representation can be selected and transformation between representations is needed.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Given the unique characteristics, strengths, and weaknesses of each CDM and data standard, no single global representation can be selected.
findings.effect_size: OMOP CDM and FHIR scored best overall
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Overall criteria the OMOP CDM and FHIR scored best.
findings.study_system: common data models / health data standards (systematic review)

findings.claim: The pan-African INSPIRE datahub is a FAIR cloud/on-premises research infrastructure using the OHDSI open-source stack and OMOP Common Data Model to harmonise African longitudinal population studies, ensuring FAIR data via metadata flows and provenance capture in a machine- and human-readable Implementation Guide.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The INSPIRE datahub, part of the Implementation Network for Sharing Population Information from Research Entities (INSPIRE), employs the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) open-source stack of tools and the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model (CDM) to harmonise data from African longitudinal population studies.
findings.study_system: African longitudinal population health data (LMIC)

findings.claim: ROBOKOP v1.0 is an open-source, modular biomedical knowledge graph system whose ORION pipeline standardizes, integrates and harmonizes heterogeneous knowledge sources into interoperable KGs using the community-developed Biolink Model schema and upper-level biomedical ontology.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A custom software pipeline termed Operational Routine for the Ingest and Output of Networks (ORION) standardizes, integrates, and harmonizes ROBOKOP's knowledge sources as interoperable KGs by leveraging the community-developed Biolink Model's universal KG schema and upper-level biomedical ontology.
findings.study_system: biomedical knowledge graph (ROBOKOP)

findings.claim: ClinGen's API-based microservices expose findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable and AI-ready human genetic variant data, providing a foundation for next-generation software, AI systems and variant-classification workflows.
findings.claim_source_sentence: By exposing findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable, and AI-ready variant data, ClinGen lays a foundation for next-generation software applications, AI systems, and variant classification workflows.
findings.study_system: clinical genomics variant knowledge (ClinGen)

findings.claim: The Semantic Units Framework is a technology-agnostic representational approach that treats statements as first-class semantic units to support FAIR and CLEAR knowledge infrastructures, enabling both machine-actionable reasoning and human-interpretable representation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Rather than proposing a new graph technology, the Semantic Units Framework provides a reusable conceptual foundation that can be realized across existing data and knowledge representation technologies and supports both machine-actionable reasoning and human-interpretable knowledge representation.
findings.study_system: knowledge representation / semantic modeling

findings.claim: The Rosetta Statement approach models natural-language statements to lower the entry barrier for FAIR knowledge graph construction, letting domain experts without formal semantics training define RDF schemata and build FAIR KGs (implemented in the Open Research Knowledge Graph).
findings.claim_source_sentence: We argue that this three-step procedure is designed to substantially lower the entry barrier for knowledge graph construction while increasing their cognitive interoperability, consistent with the CLEAR Principle.
findings.study_system: knowledge graph construction (ORKG)

findings.claim: An ontology-based electronic laboratory notebook framework (Herbie) captures complex synchrotron nano-CT beamline metadata and automatically validates and semantically annotates it so that entered data meets FAIR requirements at the point of creation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We illustrate how Herbie converts all semantic documents into a user interface, ensuring that the entered data automatically meets all FAIR requirements.
findings.study_system: synchrotron nano-CT measurement metadata

findings.claim: The SPHN Connector enables federated, source-local construction of validated, semantically enriched RDF knowledge graphs from heterogeneous health data, implementing the FAIR principles at national scale while keeping data governance at the source.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The Swiss Personalized Health Network has developed a comprehensive semantic interoperability framework to implement the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles at a national level.
findings.study_system: Swiss national health data (SPHN)

findings.claim: pyBiodatafuse is a modular query-based Python tool that integrates disparate biomedical databases into context-specific knowledge graphs, harmonizing heterogeneous formats and reducing data-wrangling burden for interoperable analyses.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To address these issues, we introduce pyBiodatafuse, a query-based Python tool designed to integrate biomedical databases.
findings.study_system: biomedical database integration

findings.claim: A comprehensive FAIR assessment of the low-carbon energy research domain screened 80 representative databases using automated and manual tests, documenting the state of the art and bottlenecks from both human and machine perspectives.
findings.claim_source_sentence: 80 databases representative for data needed to support the low carbon energy transition are screened.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: 80 databases representative for data needed to support the low carbon energy transition are screened.
findings.study_system: low-carbon energy databases

findings.claim: The ORMIR community provides practical guidelines for open and reproducible musculoskeletal imaging research, redefining study outputs as a combination of data, code and publication and recommending a folder/file structure that reflects these three outcomes.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Next, we redefine the outputs of a computational research study as-ideally-a combination of data, code, and a publication, recommend a folder and file structure that reflects these three study outcomes, and describe how to maintain and update such a structure during the study and at study publication.
findings.study_system: musculoskeletal imaging research community

findings.claim: The DataDesc metadata schema extension plus the ioProc workflow manager annotate data models in both software interfaces and datasets and automatically identify transformation requirements, bridging abstract FAIR guidelines and researchers' daily data- and software-driven analyses.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, this article bridges the gap between abstract guidelines, such as the findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability (FAIR) principles, and researchers' daily data- and software-driven analyses, promoting reusability, reproducibility, and transparency in science.
findings.study_system: coupled research software and data (energy systems)

findings.claim: AiiDAlab, a Jupyter-based web platform powered by the AiiDA infrastructure, manages and automates computational workflows with full provenance tracking and integrates with electronic laboratory notebooks for FAIR-compliant data management.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To address these challenges, we developed AiiDAlab, a Jupyter-based web platform powered by the AiiDA computational infrastructure that provides a framework for managing and automating computational workflows while ensuring reproducibility through full provenance tracking.
findings.study_system: computational workflow platform (AiiDA)

findings.claim: A computational reproducibility framework lets scientists proactively generate a complete reproducible trace as analysis unfolds and share data, methods and executable tools as part of each publication, enabling others to verify and re-execute the investigation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This article discusses the guiding principles of a computational reproducibility framework that enables a scientist to proactively generate a complete reproducible trace as analysis unfolds, and share data, methods and executable tools as part of a scientific publication, allowing other researchers to verify results and easily re-execute the steps of the scientific investigation.
findings.study_system: computational reproducibility (open science)

findings.claim: Cheminformatics evolved from proprietary closed systems toward open science, with national research-data-management infrastructure (NFDI4Chem) and increasing FAIR adoption reinforcing data sharing and reuse, though resistance to sharing and funding sustainability remain challenges.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The increasing adoption of the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles has further reinforced data sharing and reuse in computational chemistry.
findings.study_system: cheminformatics field (open-science evolution)

findings.claim: CytoTable harmonizes single-cell image-based profiling data that otherwise suffer from inconsistent schemas, inefficient file formats and undocumented ontological relationships, improving reproducibility of high-content imaging analyses.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These datasets suffer from inconsistent schemas, inefficient file formats, and undocumented ontological relationships.
findings.study_system: single-cell high-content imaging data

findings.claim: A digital, data-centric methodology integrating HPC, machine learning and knowledge engineering establishes data and information standards to ensure interoperability across the diverse tools used in nanomaterials multiscale simulation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The integration of methodologies rooted in knowledge and structured information management serves as a foundational element, establishing a framework for representing materials-related information and ensuring interoperability across a diverse range of tools.
findings.study_system: nanomaterials multiscale simulation infrastructure

findings.claim: MCPmed adapts the Model Context Protocol to bioinformatics web-server backends as a standardized, machine-actionable metadata layer that explicitly links service endpoints to scientific concepts, enhancing automation, reproducibility and interoperability for LLM- and agent-driven discovery.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We address this gap by adapting model context protocol (MCP) to bioinformatics web server backends, a standardized, machine-actionable layer that explicitly associates web service endpoints with scientific concepts and detailed metadata.
findings.study_system: bioinformatics web services (GEO, STRING, UCSC)

findings.claim: The AGENT project integrated dispersed European genebank phenotypic and genotypic data for wheat and barley through the Plant Breeding API (BrAPI), using embedded unique identifiers to transparently link distributed data entities via a BrAPI proxy.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The advantages of BrAPI in transparently linking distributed data entities through embedded, unique identifiers are highlighted.
findings.study_system: European genebank wheat/barley data

findings.claim: Indigenous Data Sovereignty considerations, combined with implementation-science frameworks (CFIR and ERIC), can guide the design of digital health technologies that respect the data interests and priorities of Indigenous Peoples.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Through a multi-year research collaborative between the University of California, San Diego and the Native BioData Consortium, it became clear that the use of an implementation science framework might guide the design of emerging digital health technologies best respecting the interests and priorities of Indigenous Peoples.
findings.study_system: Indigenous health data governance (US)

findings.claim: US natural-science-collections community consultations identified eight major themes for a national center to manage, unify and digitally expand specimen/sample data infrastructure, including ethical collaboration with Indigenous communities and broad digital access to collections data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Community consultations identified eight major themes that a center could encompass to manage, unify, and strategically expand the vast specimen/sample infrastructure and associated data stored in biological collections, address challenges facing physical biodiversity collections, and, importantly, coordinate across diverse research and education sectors.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Community consultations identified eight major themes that a center could encompass to manage, unify, and strategically expand the vast specimen/sample infrastructure and associated data stored in biological collections, address challenges facing physical biodiversity collections, and, importantly, coordinate across diverse research and education sectors.
findings.study_system: US natural science collections

findings.claim: Analyzing 531,889 PLOS and BMC articles, data availability statements became near-universal after mandates, but only a minority linked to data in a repository; articles whose statements linked to data in a repository had up to 25.36% higher average citation impact.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We also find an association between articles that include statements that link to data in a repository and up to 25.36% (± 1.07%) higher citation impact on average, using a citation prediction model.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We also find an association between articles that include statements that link to data in a repository and up to 25.36% (± 1.07%) higher citation impact on average, using a citation prediction model.
findings.study_system: PLOS and BMC journal articles (531,889)

findings.claim: A scoping review of interventions to incentivise research data sharing screened 1128 papers and included 38, identifying seven major intervention themes (publisher policies, metrics, software, sharing agreements, open-science badges, funder mandates and initiatives) and stressing the need for disciplinary data champions, proper resourcing and robust technical infrastructure.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A total of 1128 papers were screened, with 38 items being included.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A total of 1128 papers were screened, with 38 items being included.
findings.study_system: scoping review of data-sharing incentive interventions

findings.claim: Applying the Scholix/Scholexplorer framework to University of Bath outputs vastly expanded known article-dataset links; availability of author names increased from 2.4% to 89.2%, enabling detection of data reuse, but of ten reuse cases identified only three were formally cited in the references.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Availability of author names for research outputs increased from 2.4% to 89.2%, which enabled identification of ten articles reusing non-Bath-affiliated datasets published in external repositories in the first phase, giving valuable evidence of data reuse and impact for data producers.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Availability of author names for research outputs increased from 2.4% to 89.2%, which enabled identification of ten articles reusing non-Bath-affiliated datasets published in external repositories in the first phase, giving valuable evidence of data reuse and impact for data producers.
findings.study_system: University of Bath research outputs (Scholix/Scholexplorer)

findings.claim: Of 1,340 Spanish COVID-19 papers published in 2020, 87.5% had no research data and only 12.5% shared data - with just 2.1% deposited in repositories - revealing researchers' poor knowledge of how to properly share research data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A total of 12.5% share their research data of which 2.1% share their data in repositories, 5% share their data through a simple request, 0.2% do not have permission to share their data, and 5.2% share their data as supplementary material.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A total of 12.5% share their research data of which 2.1% share their data in repositories, 5% share their data through a simple request, 0.2% do not have permission to share their data, and 5.2% share their data as supplementary material.
findings.study_system: Spanish COVID-19 papers (2020)

findings.claim: A case-study audit of 23 Heliyon papers flagged for SEM descriptor mismatches (from a preprint reporting ~2400 such cases) found only two with unequivocal text-vs-figure discord but 16 of 23 with no methodological description of SEM at all, illustrating widespread incompleteness of metadata/methods descriptors that passed peer review.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Only two papers showed an unequivocal discord between textual and figure descriptors related to SEM at the level of model and maker, while 16 of the 23 papers had no methodological description of SEM in the methods section.
findings.effect_size: 16 of 23 papers had no SEM methods description
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Only two papers showed an unequivocal discord between textual and figure descriptors related to SEM at the level of model and maker, while 16 of the 23 papers had no methodological description of SEM in the methods section.
findings.study_system: Heliyon SEM-based papers (metadata/methods completeness)

findings.claim: A scoping review of biobanking and genomic research in LMICs (154 studies from 2,390 records) identified four interdependent structural gaps - infrastructure, interoperability, human-capital/data-stewardship, and governance - underpinning a biospecimen-data divide, and proposed the DIGS Model centering LMIC leadership in data governance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Four interdependent structural gaps underpin the biospecimen-data divide: (1) infrastructure gap, reflecting constraints on data generation and flow; (2) interoperability gap, arising from incompatible systems that create data silos; (3) human-capital gap, marked by limited availability of personnel with combined laboratory and data stewardship expertise; (4) governance gap, defined by weak ethical and regulatory structures.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: After deduplication (n = 880), title and abstract screening (n = 1510), and full-text review (n = 296), 154 studies were included in the final synthesis.
findings.study_system: biobanking/genomic research in LMICs (scoping review)

findings.claim: The e!DAL / Plant Genomic and Phenomics Research Data Repository (ELIXIR Germany/de.NBI) uses a 'bring the infrastructure to the data' approach that keeps research data in place wrapped in FAIR-aware software, providing FAIR-compliant services for high-throughput plant data not covered by established core databases.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To share these potentially dark data in a FAIR way and master these challenges the ELIXIR Germany/de.NBI service Plant Genomic and Phenomics Research Data Repository (PGP) implements a "bring the infrastructure to the data" approach, which allows research data to be kept in place and wrapped in a FAIR-aware software infrastructure.
findings.study_system: plant genomics/phenomics research data (e!DAL/PGP, ELIXIR Germany)

findings.claim: CODECHECK, an open-science initiative for independent execution of the computations underlying research articles during peer review, was demonstrated with 25 reproductions of diverse publications, showing that asking for reproducible workflows during collaborative review effectively improves executability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In collaboration with academic publishers and conferences, we demonstrate CODECHECK with 25 reproductions of diverse scientific publications.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In collaboration with academic publishers and conferences, we demonstrate CODECHECK with 25 reproductions of diverse scientific publications.
findings.study_system: computational reproductions during peer review (CODECHECK)

findings.claim: Traumatic brain injury translation is framed as a big-data problem dominated by data variety, where pulling unpublished 'dark data' and small long-tail datasets and making TBI resources more FAIR through better data stewardship could accelerate discovery and translation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Making TBI data resources more Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) through better data stewardship has great potential to accelerate discovery and translation for the silent epidemic of TBI.
findings.study_system: traumatic brain injury research data (dark data / long-tail)

findings.claim: Responsible data sharing in psychology requires overcoming barriers around data ownership, participant confidentiality, credit, metadata/codebooks and provenance; the authors argue research data and program code are scientific contributions that should be cited like publications and their creators formally recognized.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We argue that research data and program code are important scientific contributions that should be cited in the same way as publications.
findings.study_system: psychology research data sharing

findings.claim: To overcome the lack of incentives for publishing biodiversity data, the authors propose the 'biodiversity data paper' - publishing rich, citable metadata as academic papers - as a mechanism to give data publishers scholarly recognition, piloted by GBIF with Pensoft journals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We propose the establishment of the 'biodiversity data paper' as one possible mechanism to offer scholarly recognition for efforts and investment by data publishers in authoring rich metadata and publishing them as citable academic papers.
findings.study_system: biodiversity data publishing (GBIF/Pensoft data papers)

findings.claim: Even when publications include data-availability pledges, actual public data sharing rarely follows: only a small fraction of papers both promise and deliver open data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A study analyzing 7,750 biomedical research papers published between 2015 and 2020 found that only 9% of all papers pledged to make their data publicly available, and a mere 3% of the total followed through with this commitment [].
findings.effect_size: 9% pledged public data availability; 3% actually followed through
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A study analyzing 7,750 biomedical research papers published between 2015 and 2020 found that only 9% of all papers pledged to make their data publicly available, and a mere 3% of the total followed through with this commitment [].
findings.study_system: biomedical research papers (2015-2020); data transparency
findings.evidence: Body (Introduction) of a PLOS Medicine analysis of the data transparency crisis, quantifying the gap between data-sharing pledges and delivery.

findings.claim: An international Delphi consensus (OSIRIS) distilled a core set of reproducibility items from a larger candidate pool, providing a standardized checklist for reporting.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Briefly, the Delphi study (two online surveys and one online meeting) led to the inclusion of 31 items out of the 44 items initially considered ().
findings.effect_size: 31 of 44 candidate items retained (32 core items after one split)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Briefly, the Delphi study (two online surveys and one online meeting) led to the inclusion of 31 items out of the 44 items initially considered ().
findings.study_system: Delphi consensus process on reproducibility reporting items
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of the OSIRIS international consensus paper on core reproducibility items.

findings.claim: A cross-disciplinary interview study of European researchers found reproducibility is shaped by data-quality, documentation, infrastructure, resourcing and disciplinary-norm barriers rather than technical fixes alone.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of 249 invited researchers, 60 agreed and were interviewed.
findings.effect_size: 60 interviewees of 249 invited across disciplines and career stages
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of 249 invited researchers, 60 agreed and were interviewed.
findings.study_system: cross-disciplinary qualitative interviews with researchers in Europe
findings.evidence: Body (Methods/Results) of a qualitative interview study on what helps and hinders reproducible research.

findings.claim: In oncology data reuse, patients prioritise better care and a sense of societal contribution, while professionals emphasise data accuracy, purpose limitation and peer-reviewed dissemination.
findings.claim_source_sentence: At individual level, they considered most important 1) the opportunity to receive better care (which included e.g., saving the patient’s life, better health, better interaction with physicians, improved quality of life) and 2) feeling satisfaction from being able to contribute to society by sharing their data.
findings.study_system: cancer patients, patient representatives and health professionals, EU (EHDS context)
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of a multi-stakeholder qualitative study on patient values in data reuse for the European Health Data Space.

findings.claim: The absence of adopted, standardized data-reporting practices (including a unified anatomical atlas and consistent metadata) is a core reproducibility and data-reuse bottleneck, exemplified in zebrafish research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The lack of an annotated unified anatomical atlas is a bottleneck; creating one would resolve long-standing challenges in cross-study comparisons of imaging data, eliminating ambiguity in data interpretation and facilitating cross-study comparisons.
findings.study_system: zebrafish research data; standardized reporting and metadata integration
findings.evidence: Body of a perspective arguing that standardized data reporting and metadata integration are prerequisites for FAIR reuse and reproducibility.

findings.claim: Data reuse in global health is impeded by heavy upstream data-cleaning and curation burdens that consume most analyst time before analysis can begin.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A geospatial analyst working in Laos, Myanmar and Thailand described spending ‘80% of their time curating data before they could start analysing it’, citing repeated efforts to resolve inconsistencies.
findings.effect_size: 80% of analyst time spent curating data before analysis
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A geospatial analyst working in Laos, Myanmar and Thailand described spending ‘80% of their time curating data before they could start analysing it’, citing repeated efforts to resolve inconsistencies.
findings.study_system: global health data actors (policy, funding, research); qualitative interviews
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of an interview study on data reuse in global health, most participants LMIC-based.

findings.claim: Instruments used to measure data-sharing knowledge, attitudes and practices are themselves frequently not shared, undermining reuse and comparison of survey evidence.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of the 60 survey instruments, 24 publications (40%) did not include the entire survey in the manuscript, and we emailed the respective authors to request the missing surveys.
findings.effect_size: 40% (24/60) did not publish the full instrument; only 11 (18%) shared on request
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of the 60 survey instruments, 24 publications (40%) did not include the entire survey in the manuscript, and we emailed the respective authors to request the missing surveys.
findings.study_system: measurement systematic review of biomedical data-sharing KAP surveys
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of a measurement systematic review quantifying availability of the survey instruments themselves.

findings.claim: LinkML is an open, ontology-aware data modeling framework that assigns persistent identifiers to schema elements and translates schemas across formats, supporting FAIR-aligned data models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The LinkML framework provides a flexible data modeling language built around 4 core element types: schemas, classes, slots, and enumerations.
findings.effect_size: >400 GitHub stars; software cloned hundreds of times per week
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The software is cloned hundreds of times a week, and the main LinkML GitHub repository has over 400 stars as of October 2025.
findings.study_system: open-source data modeling framework (software adoption)
findings.evidence: Body of the LinkML framework paper describing its metamodel, persistent identifiers, and adoption metrics.

findings.claim: ClarID encodes biomedical metadata (study, species, subject, sample type, ICD-10 condition, provenance) into compact human-readable identifiers to support FAIR metadata integration and cross-repository harmonization.
findings.claim_source_sentence: An example of ClarID in human format is ‘TARGET_AML-HomSap-00002-BMR-PRI-NAV-C92.0-COL-P0N’, where each component encodes a specific attribute: BMR, bone marrow; PRI, primary tumor site; C92.0, ICD-10 code for acute myeloblastic leukemia (AML); COL, collection time; and P0N, duration not available.
findings.study_system: Genomic Data Commons clinical metadata; identifier specification
findings.evidence: Body (Results) of the ClarID specification paper demonstrating subject-level encoding of GDC metadata.

findings.claim: Adopting the ISO/IEC 11179 metadata registry standard is presented as automatically supporting FAIR adherence (findability, interoperability, reusability) for cross-border NCD indicator comparison.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The concepts of the ISO/IEC 11179 metadata model automatically serve to make data adhere to FAIR data principles (), especially those addressing findability, interoperability, and reusability.
findings.study_system: EU non-communicable disease indicator framework (CHIEF/SOLICIT); metadata standards
findings.evidence: Body of a feasibility study using ISO/IEC 11179 plus ontologies to build a FAIR NCD indicator vault.

findings.claim: CMEO, a metadata-centric ontology, harmonizes variable-level metadata across 50+ multinational cardiovascular studies, addressing the lack of formal semantic relationships in generic registry standards.
findings.claim_source_sentence: CMEO has been developed and deployed within the context of the iCARE4CVD (Improved Cardiovascular Risk Stratification through Personalized Remote and Digital Interventions) initiative [,], which aims to standardize and harmonize metadata across more than 50 cardiovascular studies.
findings.effect_size: harmonization across more than 50 studies; over 30 partners
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The project brings together over 30 partners across academia, industry, and healthcare systems to enable the reuse and integration of real-world data from more than 50 multi-national observational and interventional studies.
findings.study_system: cardiovascular studies metadata harmonization (iCARE4CVD consortium)
findings.evidence: Body (Methods) of the CMEO ontology paper describing deployment scope and rationale relative to ISO/IEC 11179.

findings.claim: A leading medical journal introduced a mandatory code-sharing policy to strengthen reproducibility and accountability by making author-generated code openly available at publication.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Today, we are proud to announce the rollout of our code-sharing policy—a concrete step toward strengthening reproducibility and accountability in medical research by ensuring that the code underlying published findings is shared openly and responsibly.
findings.study_system: journal editorial policy (medical research); code sharing
findings.evidence: Editorial announcing a journal code-sharing mandate (retrieved text <15KB, treated as abstract_only).

findings.claim: Reproduction is rarely the stated purpose of clinical-trial data-reuse requests, and independent reanalyses frequently reach conclusions differing from the original trials.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For instance, a review of 172 data requests to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute’s Biologic Specimen and Data Repository Information Coordinating Center between 2000 and 2016 found that only 2 (1%) were for the purpose of reproduction analyses [].
findings.effect_size: 2 of 172 (1%) data requests were for reproduction analyses
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For instance, a review of 172 data requests to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute’s Biologic Specimen and Data Repository Information Coordinating Center between 2000 and 2016 found that only 2 (1%) were for the purpose of reproduction analyses [].
findings.study_system: clinical trial data repository requests; reanalysis datathon (rectal carcinoma RCT)
findings.evidence: Body (Introduction) of a case study on supporting reanalysis and reuse of clinical trial data via a multi-team datathon.

findings.claim: Mondo integrates disease terminology across communities by reconciling many overlapping source resources into a single logic-based, harmonized disease ontology, supporting interoperability of disease annotations.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Mondo is a logic-based ontology that reconciles 21 disease resources (), collectively representing approximately 100,000 source concepts, into >25,000 distinct disease concepts for both humans (>22,000) and nonhuman animals (∼3,000) ().
findings.effect_size: 21 source resources / ~100,000 source concepts reconciled into >25,000 disease concepts
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Mondo is a logic-based ontology that reconciles 21 disease resources (), collectively representing approximately 100,000 source concepts, into >25,000 distinct disease concepts for both humans (>22,000) and nonhuman animals (∼3,000) ().
findings.study_system: disease terminology integration ontology (Mondo)
findings.evidence: Body of the Mondo paper describing the scope of cross-resource disease terminology reconciliation.

findings.claim: A unified discovery portal improves dataset findability by aggregating and ontology-harmonizing metadata from millions of datasets across dozens of repositories.
findings.claim_source_sentence: As of this writing, the Discovery Portal aggregates and harmonizes metadata from more than 4.3 million data sets across 42 repositories.
